subproblem.title: Operator norm of an n-covector is at most P^n times a bound on its standard-basis values
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, α ∈ Covector (Euclid P) n and C ≥ 0 such that |α(e_{j(0)}, …, e_{j(n−1)})| ≤ C for every j : Fin n → Fin P, where e = EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ is the standard orthonormal basis of ℝ^P. Then the operator norm of α satisfies ‖α‖ ≤ P^n·C.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (α : Covector (Euclid P) n) (C : ℝ), 0 ≤ C → (∀ j : Fin n → Fin P, |α (fun k => EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ (j k))| ≤ C) → ‖α‖ ≤ (P : ℝ) ^ n * C
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 0(c) of the parent proof of regcomp_exists_smooth_unit_form_approx. There the bound |α(e∘j)| ≤ |α|_E for every j (from regcomp_covector_eval_orthonormal_le if j is injective, and from the alternating property if not) is fed into a multilinear expansion; here that bound is abstracted as the hypothesis C, and the parent applies this lemma with C := |α|_E. Notation: e_i := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ i; e∘r := (k ↦ e_{r(k)}) for r : Fin n → Fin P; w_i denotes the i-th coordinate of w ∈ Euclid P; ‖α‖ is the Mathlib (operator) norm of Covector (Euclid P) n.

1. (Reduction.) Since P^n·C ≥ 0, by ContinuousAlternatingMap.opNorm_le_bound it suffices to show |α(v)| ≤ P^n·C·Π_k ‖v_k‖ for every v : Fin n → Euclid P.

2. (Basis expansion.) Every w ∈ Euclid P satisfies w = Σ_{i : Fin P} w_i • e_i (OrthonormalBasis.sum_repr together with EuclideanSpace.basisFun_repr, which identifies the basis coordinates of w with its coordinates w_i). Apply this to each v_k.

3. (Multilinear expansion.) By multilinearity of α in each of its n arguments (ContinuousMultilinearMap.map_sum applied to α.toContinuousMultilinearMap, or ContinuousAlternatingMap.map_sum), α(v) = Σ_{r : Fin n → Fin P} α(k ↦ (v_k)_{r(k)} • e_{r(k)}). Pulling the scalars out of all slots (ContinuousMultilinearMap.map_smul_univ), α(k ↦ (v_k)_{r(k)} • e_{r(k)}) = (Π_k (v_k)_{r(k)})·α(e∘r). Hence α(v) = Σ_r (Π_k (v_k)_{r(k)})·α(e∘r).

4. (Coordinate bound.) For w ∈ Euclid P and i : Fin P, |w_i| ≤ ‖w‖ (PiLp.norm_apply_le; equivalently w_i² ≤ Σ_l w_l² = ‖w‖²).

5. (Estimate.) By the triangle inequality (norm_sum_le), |Π_k a_k| = Π_k |a_k| (Finset.abs_prod), step 4 together with monotonicity of finite products of nonnegative reals, and the hypothesis |α(e∘r)| ≤ C:
 |α(v)| ≤ Σ_r (Π_k |(v_k)_{r(k)}|)·|α(e∘r)| ≤ Σ_r (Π_k ‖v_k‖)·C = #(Fin n → Fin P)·C·Π_k ‖v_k‖ = P^n·C·Π_k ‖v_k‖,
 where #(Fin n → Fin P) = P^n (Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fun, Fintype.card_fin). This is the bound required in step 1, so ‖α‖ ≤ P^n·C. ∎

(The same argument covers the degenerate cases: for n = 0 the only r is the empty tuple and empty products equal 1; for P = 0 < n the index set of r is empty, so α(v) = 0 ≤ 0.)
proof_key_steps: Expand each v_k in the standard basis and use multilinearity: α(v) = Σ_r (Π_k (v_k)_{r(k)})·α(e∘r).
Bound |(v_k)_i| ≤ ‖v_k‖ and |α(e∘r)| ≤ C, and count the P^n tuples r.

audit.reason: The standard-basis multilinear expansion, coordinate bounds and P^n tuple count prove the required evaluation bound, which opNorm_le_bound converts to the exact conclusion. C ≥ 0 is used correctly in the estimates. Empty-index cases are valid. No undeclared dependency or circular step occurs.

subproblem.title: Radial retraction onto the closed unit ball is nonexpansive towards points of the ball
subproblem.statement: Let E be a real inner product space and x, y ∈ E with ‖y‖ ≤ 1. Then ‖(max 1 ‖x‖)⁻¹ • x − y‖ ≤ ‖x − y‖.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (E : Type) [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] (x y : E), ‖y‖ ≤ 1 → ‖(max 1 ‖x‖)⁻¹ • x - y‖ ≤ ‖x - y‖
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 0(d) of the parent proof of regcomp_exists_smooth_unit_form_approx. There the computation is carried out in the inner product space EuclideanSpace ℝ N with x := Φ(v), y := Φ(b); here it is stated for an arbitrary real inner product space E. Write ⟨·,·⟩ for the real inner product.

1. (Case ‖x‖ ≤ 1.) Then max 1 ‖x‖ = 1, so (max 1 ‖x‖)⁻¹ • x = 1 • x = x and both sides are equal.

2. (Case s := ‖x‖ > 1: expansion.) Then max 1 ‖x‖ = s and s > 0, and the claim reads ‖s⁻¹ • x − y‖ ≤ ‖x − y‖. By norm_sub_sq_real (‖a − b‖² = ‖a‖² − 2⟨a, b⟩ + ‖b‖²), norm_smul and inner_smul_left (with |s⁻¹| = s⁻¹ and s⁻¹·s = 1):
 ‖x − y‖² = s² − 2⟨x, y⟩ + ‖y‖²,
 ‖s⁻¹ • x − y‖² = (s⁻¹s)² − 2s⁻¹⟨x, y⟩ + ‖y‖² = 1 − 2s⁻¹⟨x, y⟩ + ‖y‖².

3. (Difference.) Subtracting, ‖x − y‖² − ‖s⁻¹ • x − y‖² = s² − 1 − 2(1 − s⁻¹)⟨x, y⟩.

4. (Sign.) By Cauchy–Schwarz (real_inner_le_norm) and ‖y‖ ≤ 1, ⟨x, y⟩ ≤ ‖x‖‖y‖ ≤ s. Since s > 1, s⁻¹ < 1 (inv_lt_one_of_one_lt₀), i.e. 1 − s⁻¹ > 0. Multiplying, 2(1 − s⁻¹)⟨x, y⟩ ≤ 2(1 − s⁻¹)s = 2s − 2. Hence the difference in step 3 is at least s² − 1 − (2s − 2) = (s − 1)² ≥ 0 (nlinarith with these facts closes this).

5. (Conclusion.) Thus ‖s⁻¹ • x − y‖² ≤ ‖x − y‖², and as both norms are nonnegative, ‖s⁻¹ • x − y‖ ≤ ‖x − y‖ (sq_le_sq₀). ∎
proof_key_steps: If ‖x‖ ≤ 1 the retraction is the identity and equality holds.
If s = ‖x‖ > 1, expand both squared distances (norm_sub_sq_real): their difference is s² − 1 − 2(1 − 1/s)⟨x, y⟩.
Cauchy–Schwarz ⟨x, y⟩ ≤ s and 1 − 1/s > 0 give difference ≥ (s − 1)² ≥ 0; take square roots.

audit.reason: The prose and Lean type agree. The two norm cases are exhaustive. For s > 1, the squared-distance expansion and Cauchy–Schwarz give difference at least (s − 1)²; nonnegativity of norms yields the stated inequality. The proof is complete and independent.

subproblem.title: The Euclidean coefficient norm is a continuous seminorm dominated by the operator norm, with nonexpansive radial retraction
subproblem.statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ there is a constant c > 0 such that, writing |α|_E := covectorEuclideanNorm α for α ∈ Covector (Euclid P) n and ‖α‖ for the operator norm: (i) α ↦ |α|_E is continuous; (ii) |α + β|_E ≤ |α|_E + |β|_E for all α, β; (iii) |t•α|_E = |t|·|α|_E for all t ∈ ℝ and α; (iv) |α|_E ≤ c·‖α‖ for all α; (v) for all v, b with |b|_E ≤ 1, |(max 1 |v|_E)⁻¹ • v − b|_E ≤ |v − b|_E.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ), ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ Continuous (fun α : Covector (Euclid P) n => covectorEuclideanNorm α) ∧ (∀ α β : Covector (Euclid P) n, covectorEuclideanNorm (α + β) ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α + covectorEuclideanNorm β) ∧ (∀ (t : ℝ) (α : Covector (Euclid P) n), covectorEuclideanNorm (t • α) = |t| * covectorEuclideanNorm α) ∧ (∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, covectorEuclideanNorm α ≤ c * ‖α‖) ∧ ∀ v b : Covector (Euclid P) n, covectorEuclideanNorm b ≤ 1 → covectorEuclideanNorm ((max 1 (covectorEuclideanNorm v))⁻¹ • v - b) ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm (v - b)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 0 of the parent proof of regcomp_exists_smooth_unit_form_approx: its first paragraph (the coefficient map Φ) and items (a), (b), (d). Uses the sibling lemma regcomp_norm_radial_retraction_sub_le. Notation: e_i := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ i (i : Fin P) is the standard orthonormal basis of ℝ^P = Euclid P; for j : Fin n → Fin P, e∘j := (k ↦ e_{j(k)}) : Fin n → Euclid P; N := Fin n → Fin P (a finite type); Λ^n := Covector (Euclid P) n = Euclid P [⋀^Fin n]→L[ℝ] ℝ with its operator norm ‖·‖; by definition (SimonGMT Chapter06/Mass.lean) |α|_E = covectorEuclideanNorm α = √(Σ_{j : N} (if StrictMono j then α(e∘j)² else 0)).

1. (Coordinate functionals.) For a fixed tuple m : Fin n → Euclid P, evaluation α ↦ α(m) is a continuous linear functional on Λ^n (linear because the operations on alternating maps are pointwise; continuous since |α(m)| ≤ ‖α‖·Π_k ‖m_k‖); in Mathlib it is ContinuousAlternatingMap.apply ℝ (Euclid P) ℝ m : Λ^n →L[ℝ] ℝ. For j : N let ev_j : Λ^n →L[ℝ] ℝ be evaluation at e∘j if j is strictly increasing and 0 otherwise (classical case split on StrictMono j). So ev_j(α) = α(e∘j) if StrictMono j and ev_j(α) = 0 otherwise.

2. (Coefficient map.) Let Φ := (EuclideanSpace.equiv N ℝ).symm ∘L ContinuousLinearMap.pi (fun j ↦ ev_j) : Λ^n →L[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ N. Here EuclideanSpace.equiv N ℝ is the continuous linear equivalence EuclideanSpace ℝ N ≃ (N → ℝ) that keeps coordinates. Φ is continuous linear, and the j-th coordinate of Φ(α) is ev_j(α).

3. (Norm identity ‖Φ(α)‖ = |α|_E.) By EuclideanSpace.norm_eq, ‖Φ(α)‖ = √(Σ_{j : N} ‖Φ(α)_j‖²) = √(Σ_j ev_j(α)²), since ‖t‖² = t² for t ∈ ℝ. For each j the summands agree. If StrictMono j, then ev_j(α)² = α(e∘j)² = (if StrictMono j then α(e∘j)² else 0). Otherwise ev_j(α)² = 0 = (if StrictMono j then α(e∘j)² else 0). So the radicands are equal (Finset.sum_congr) and ‖Φ(α)‖ = |α|_E for every α. (Lean shape: rw [EuclideanSpace.norm_eq, covectorEuclideanNorm]; congr 1; Finset.sum_congr; split_ifs with hj; simp [EuclideanSpace.equiv, hj].)

4. (The five properties, with c := 1 + ‖Φ‖ > 0.) Each property below is rewritten through step 3.
 (i) Continuity. The function α ↦ |α|_E equals α ↦ ‖Φ(α)‖ (funext with step 3), which is continuous as a composition of the continuous Φ with the norm (continuous_norm.comp Φ.continuous).
 (ii) Triangle inequality. |α + β|_E = ‖Φ(α) + Φ(β)‖ ≤ ‖Φ(α)‖ + ‖Φ(β)‖ = |α|_E + |β|_E (map_add, norm_add_le).
 (iii) Homogeneity. |t•α|_E = ‖t • Φ(α)‖ = |t|·‖Φ(α)‖ = |t|·|α|_E (map_smul, norm_smul, Real.norm_eq_abs).
 (iv) Comparison with the operator norm. |α|_E = ‖Φ(α)‖ ≤ ‖Φ‖·‖α‖ ≤ (1 + ‖Φ‖)·‖α‖ (ContinuousLinearMap.le_opNorm and ‖α‖ ≥ 0).
 (v) Radial retraction. Let v, b ∈ Λ^n with |b|_E ≤ 1, and put m := max 1 |v|_E = max 1 ‖Φ(v)‖. By linearity, Φ(m⁻¹ • v − b) = (max 1 ‖Φ(v)‖)⁻¹ • Φ(v) − Φ(b) and Φ(v − b) = Φ(v) − Φ(b). Apply regcomp_norm_radial_retraction_sub_le in the real inner product space E := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n → Fin P) with x := Φ(v) and y := Φ(b), noting ‖y‖ = |b|_E ≤ 1. It gives ‖(max 1 ‖Φ(v)‖)⁻¹ • Φ(v) − Φ(b)‖ ≤ ‖Φ(v) − Φ(b)‖, that is, |m⁻¹ • v − b|_E ≤ |v − b|_E by step 3.
Hence c = 1 + ‖Φ‖ satisfies 0 < c and (i)–(v). ∎
proof_key_steps: For each j : Fin n → Fin P, ev_j (evaluation at (e_{j(0)}, …, e_{j(n−1)}) if j is strictly increasing, else 0) is a continuous linear functional on Covector (Euclid P) n.
Φ := (EuclideanSpace.equiv N ℝ).symm ∘L ContinuousLinearMap.pi ev satisfies ‖Φ α‖ = covectorEuclideanNorm α (EuclideanSpace.norm_eq, termwise comparison).
With c := 1 + ‖Φ‖: continuity, triangle inequality and homogeneity come from Φ and the norm; |α|_E ≤ ‖Φ‖‖α‖ ≤ c‖α‖.
The retraction inequality is regcomp_norm_radial_retraction_sub_le applied to x = Φ v, y = Φ b in EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n → Fin P).

audit.reason: The explicit continuous linear coefficient map has Euclidean norm exactly covectorEuclideanNorm. This proves all four seminorm/comparison clauses with c = 1 + ‖Φ‖, and the declared radial_retraction dependency proves the fifth clause. The inferred coefficient-space norm is the intended Euclidean norm. All hypotheses and conclusions match the frozen proposition.

subproblem.title: Continuous compactly supported L¹(ν)-approximation of a covector field keeping |·|_E ≤ 1 and support in O
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, ν a finite measure on ℝ^P, O ⊆ ℝ^P open, K ⊆ O compact, and g : ℝ^P → Covector (Euclid P) n ν-integrable (Bochner integrable for the operator norm) with |g(x)|_E ≤ 1 for all x and g(x) = 0 for all x ∉ K (|·|_E = covectorEuclideanNorm). Then for every ε > 0 there is a continuous f : ℝ^P → Covector (Euclid P) n with compact support, tsupport f ⊆ O, |f(z)|_E ≤ 1 for all z, and ∫⁻ ofReal(|f(x) − g(x)|_E) dν(x) ≤ ofReal(ε).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (ν : Measure (Euclid P)) (O K : Set (Euclid P)) (g : Euclid P → Covector (Euclid P) n), IsFiniteMeasure ν → IsOpen O → IsCompact K → K ⊆ O → Integrable g ν → (∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm (g x) ≤ 1) → (∀ x, x ∉ K → g x = 0) → ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ f : Euclid P → Covector (Euclid P) n, Continuous f ∧ HasCompactSupport f ∧ tsupport f ⊆ O ∧ (∀ z, covectorEuclideanNorm (f z) ≤ 1) ∧ ∫⁻ x, ENNReal.ofReal (covectorEuclideanNorm (f x - g x)) ∂ν ≤ ENNReal.ofReal ε
proof_key_steps: From regcomp_covectorEuclideanNorm_seminorm_retract: |·|_E is continuous, homogeneous and ≤ c‖·‖. The radial retraction π(v) = (max 1 |v|_E)⁻¹ • v is continuous, fixes 0, maps into the unit |·|_E-ball and is nonexpansive towards it.
ν is regular. C_c-density gives a continuous g₀ with ∫⁻ ‖g − g₀‖ₑ dν ≤ ofReal(ε/c), hence ∫⁻ ofReal|g₀ − g|_E dν ≤ ofReal ε.
Urysohn cutoff χ (1 on K, 0 off interior L, with L ⊆ O compact): g₁ = χ g₀ has support in L, and |g₁ − g|_E ≤ |g₀ − g|_E because g = χ g.
f = π ∘ g₁ is continuous, compactly supported in L ⊆ O, has |f|_E ≤ 1 and |f − g|_E ≤ |g₁ − g|_E; integrate.

audit.reason: Finite Euclidean Borel measures satisfy the required regularity assumptions, and integrability is explicitly hypothesized. Density at tolerance ε/c, the cutoff identity g = χg, and the zero-preserving radial retraction establish continuity, compact support inside O, the unit bound and the exact lower-integral estimate. All parameter signs and integral manipulations are justified; only coeff_norm_toolkit is needed.

subproblem.title: Uniform C^∞ approximation of a continuous compactly supported covector field inside its support, keeping |·|_E ≤ 1
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and f : ℝ^P → Covector (Euclid P) n continuous with compact support and |f(z)|_E ≤ 1 for all z (|·|_E = covectorEuclideanNorm). Then for every κ > 0 there is a differential n-form h : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n with IsTestForm h (C^∞ with compact support), support h ⊆ support f (Function.support, i.e. h(z) = 0 wherever f(z) = 0), |h(z)|_E ≤ 1 for all z, and |h(z) − f(z)|_E ≤ κ for all z.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (f : Euclid P → Covector (Euclid P) n), Continuous f → HasCompactSupport f → (∀ z, covectorEuclideanNorm (f z) ≤ 1) → ∀ κ : ℝ, 0 < κ → ∃ h : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n, IsTestForm h ∧ support h ⊆ support f ∧ (∀ z, covectorEuclideanNorm (h z) ≤ 1) ∧ ∀ z, covectorEuclideanNorm (h z - f z) ≤ κ
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the Remark ("equivalent implementation of step 4") of the parent proof of regcomp_exists_smooth_unit_form_approx, applied to g₂ := f. The support inclusion support h ⊆ support g₂ stated in that Remark is kept as a conclusion, and the parent's |·|_E error 2δ is made ≤ κ. Uses the sibling lemma regcomp_covectorEuclideanNorm_seminorm_retract. Implementation note: Continuous.exists_contDiff_approx lives in Mathlib.Geometry.Manifold.SmoothApprox, which is not in the import closure of GMT.Ch07.Submission; the implementation must add this import, as the parent's implementation note prescribes. Notation: Λ^n := Covector (Euclid P) n with operator norm ‖·‖ and dist(α, β) = ‖α − β‖; |·|_E := covectorEuclideanNorm; IsTestForm h means ContDiff ℝ ∞ h ∧ HasCompactSupport h.

0. (Norm facts.) By regcomp_covectorEuclideanNorm_seminorm_retract choose c > 0 such that, for all α, β ∈ Λ^n and t ∈ ℝ: (ii) |α + β|_E ≤ |α|_E + |β|_E; (iii) |t•α|_E = |t|·|α|_E (in particular |−α|_E = |α|_E, also covectorEuclideanNorm_neg); (iv) |α|_E ≤ c‖α‖.

1. (Parameter.) Let δ := min(1/2, κ/2). Then 0 < δ ≤ 1/2 (so 1 − δ ≥ 0) and 2δ ≤ κ.

2. (Smooth approximation.) The map F(x) := (1 − δ) • f(x) is continuous (Continuous.const_smul), and the constant function x ↦ δ/c is continuous and positive. Euclid P is a finite-dimensional real normed space, so Continuous.exists_contDiff_approx applies with order (⊤ : ℕ∞); its conclusion ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) h is ContDiff ℝ ∞ h. It gives h : Euclid P → Λ^n with ContDiff ℝ ∞ h, dist(h(x), F(x)) < δ/c for all x, and support h ⊆ support F.

3. (Support.) support F ⊆ support f (support_const_smul_subset: if (1 − δ)•f(x) ≠ 0 then f(x) ≠ 0), so support h ⊆ support f.

4. (Compact support.) tsupport h = closure(support h) ⊆ closure(support f) = tsupport f (closure_mono). tsupport f is compact because f has compact support, and tsupport h is closed (isClosed_tsupport). So tsupport h is compact (IsCompact.of_isClosed_subset), i.e. HasCompactSupport h. With step 2, IsTestForm h.

5. (Closeness to F.) For every x, by (iv) and dist_eq_norm, |h(x) − F(x)|_E ≤ c‖h(x) − F(x)‖ = c·dist(h(x), F(x)) < c·(δ/c) = δ.

6. (Unit bound.) h(x) = (h(x) − F(x)) + (1 − δ) • f(x). So by (ii), (iii), 1 − δ ≥ 0, step 5 and |f(x)|_E ≤ 1: |h(x)|_E ≤ |h(x) − F(x)|_E + (1 − δ)|f(x)|_E < δ + (1 − δ) = 1.

7. (Closeness to f.) h(x) − f(x) = (h(x) − F(x)) + (−(δ • f(x))). By (ii), (iii), δ > 0 and step 5: |h(x) − f(x)|_E ≤ |h(x) − F(x)|_E + δ|f(x)|_E < δ + δ = 2δ ≤ κ.

8. Steps 2–7 give IsTestForm h, support h ⊆ support f, |h(z)|_E ≤ 1 and |h(z) − f(z)|_E ≤ κ for all z. ∎
proof_key_steps: From regcomp_covectorEuclideanNorm_seminorm_retract: |·|_E is a seminorm with |α|_E ≤ c‖α‖.
With δ = min(1/2, κ/2), apply Continuous.exists_contDiff_approx (order ⊤) to (1 − δ)•f with constant precision δ/c: get a C^∞ h with support h ⊆ support f and ‖h − (1 − δ)f‖ < δ/c.
tsupport h ⊆ tsupport f is compact, so IsTestForm h.
|h − (1 − δ)f|_E < δ, hence |h|_E < δ + (1 − δ) = 1 and |h − f|_E < 2δ ≤ κ.

audit.reason: Pinned Continuous.exists_contDiff_approx supplies the stated support inclusion and C∞ regularity, requiring finite-dimensionality only of the domain. With δ = min(1/2, κ/2), the shrinking and approximation estimates establish the unit bound and error ≤ κ. Closure containment proves compact support. The proof uses only coeff_norm_toolkit and matches the exact proposition.
